exposure: concordant twin pairs (smaller twin >80% of birth weight of larger twin)
cohort: 831 obese (BMI ≥30.0 kg/m2) women delivering 1,662 liveborn, term (≥37 weeks gestation) twin infants
finding: Increasing gestational weight gain was associated with larger infants but increased risk of preeclampsia and cesarean delivery in term twin pregnancies in obese women.
mod_finding: Women who gained >42 pounds had a borderline significantly higher odds of preeclampsia than women who gained 25-42 pounds (adjusted OR 1.72; 95% CI 1.00-2.99, p = .052).
